item.title: Rapidly intensifying winter storm to strike Ontario with snow, ice, and high winds
item.description: A powerful bomb cyclone is forecast to strike Ontario bringing heavy snow, freezing rain, and severe winds from Sunday through Tuesday, December 28 to 30, 2025, as the deepening low crosses the Great Lakes. Environment and Climate Change Canada has issued Winter Storm and Freezing Rain Warnings, with snowfall totals of up to 50 cm (20 inches) and gusts exceeding 100 km/h (62 mph) expected in some areas. Source

item.title: Three killed in Sweden as Storm Johannes sweeps across Nordic countries
item.description: A powerful winter storm named Johannes swept across the Nordic countries over the weekend, killing three people in Sweden and leaving hundreds of thousands without electricity across Sweden, Norway, and Finland. Sweden’s Meteorological and Hydrological Institute (SMHI) issued widespread alerts for strong winds as the system moved north. The storm, known as Hannes in Finland, also caused major travel disruptions, grounding flights and halting rail and ferry traffic. Source

item.title: Over 30 weather-related crashes, one fatality reported as extreme cold and snow hit Iowa
item.description: The Iowa State Patrol responded to 31 crashes during extreme winter weather on December 28, 2025, as snow, high winds, and whiteout conditions spread across the state. One person was killed, and several others were injured while visibility dropped to near zero on major highways, including Interstate 35. Source

item.title: Mount Etna’s Northeast Crater erupts for the first time in 28 years, Italy
item.description: Two paroxysmal eruptions occurred at Mount Etna’s Northeast Crater on December 27, 2025, marking the first major eruptive episode from this crater in almost 28 years. The events produced lava fountains up to 500 m (1 640 feet), eruptive columns rising over 10 km (6 miles) above sea level, and a short lava flow from the nearby Voragine Crater. Activity gradually declined by December 28, with continued strombolian explosions and weak effusion. Source

item.title: Tornadoes rip through Tazewell, Christian, and Macon counties, leaving thousands without power, Illinois
item.description: Multiple tornadoes, including an EF-1 with peak winds of 158 km/h (98 mph), touched down in Illinois on Sunday, December 28, 2025, with significant damage and power outages being reported across Tazewell, Christian, and Macon counties. Source

item.title: Powerful winter storm floods Gaza, leaving 17 dead and destroying over 42 000 tents
item.description: A powerful winter storm swept across Gaza over the past seven days, leaving at least 17 people dead and over 42 000 tents destroyed by December 28, 2025. Source

item.title: Severe Tropical Cyclone Hayley forecast to make landfall over the Dampier Peninsula, Australia
item.description: Severe Tropical Cyclone Hayley is forecast to make landfall over the northern Dampier Peninsula, Western Australia, late on Tuesday, December 30, 2025, as a Category 3 system. The cyclone is expected to bring destructive winds, heavy rainfall, and flash flooding across parts of the west Kimberley coast. Source

item.title: Earth-directed CME from M4.2 flare forecast to produce G1 geomagnetic storm on New Year’s Day
item.description: A coronal mass ejection (CME) associated with an M4.2 solar flare from Region 4317 is expected to produce a G1 - Minor geomagnetic storm as it grazes Earth late on December 31 into early January 1, 2026. Source

item.title: Three killed by floods and landslides in Andalusia, Spain
item.description: At least three people have been killed by severe floods and landslides in Spain between December 28--29, 2025. Source

item.title: Subtropical moisture and re-intensified atmospheric river to impact California through New Year’s weekend
item.description: A surge of subtropical moisture is forecast to bring moderate to heavy rain to southern and central California on Wednesday, December 31, 2025, with rain spreading north on Thursday, January 1, 2026. A stronger system with a re-intensified atmospheric river is expected to make landfall early Friday, January 2, bringing heavier precipitation along the northern and central California coast. Source
